params.body:
Replaces #222. The same sign-in with Google, LinkedIn and Microsoft, carried onto today's main (it conflicted after 22 merges), with two rules added. Close #222 when this one is merged.

**What it is** (unchanged from #222). "Continue with Google / LinkedIn / Microsoft" on the sign-in and register pages, and "Sign-in methods" on the account page (add, remove, never the last way in). The Observatory and the Studio sign in through gentells.com, so they get the providers with it. Microsoft's address is believed only on the signed ID token's evidence (a personal account, or `xms_edov` with an `email` claim), never on the Graph profile a tenant admin sets. A provider without credentials has no button and its routes answer 404.

**Added 1: an existing account is joined by address only where the provider holds the mailbox.** #222 joined on "the provider confirmed the address". A provider confirms an address once, when it is added, and does not notice when the person loses the mailbox. Someone who leaves a company keeps their Google, LinkedIn or personal Microsoft account on the old work address. Joined by address, that would open the reader's or team member's account here after the company closed the mailbox, which a password reset never allows. `SocialIdentity::holdsMailbox`:
- Google: a gmail.com address, or the Workspace domain Google names in `hd` (Google's own rule for when it is authoritative for an address);
- Microsoft: a work account with `xms_edov`, or a personal account on one of Microsoft's own mail domains;
- LinkedIn: never; it keeps no mailbox.

Otherwise the person is told to sign in with their password and add the provider from the account page, which #222 already offers. A confirmed address the provider does not hold still makes a new account: nobody else's is opened.

**Added 2: through the account door behind the holding page.** #222 kept the provider routes behind the cover, so a tester with an account editorial made, and no preview link, could not use them. Since #225 `/login` and the reset links are the account door. The provider routes are now too: they open accounts that exist, and make a new one only for a visitor with a preview link (`PreLaunch::admits`).

**Carried over.** The one conflict (`PasswordResetController`: main's reset and invite link now share one closure) keeps main's shape with #222's `password_usable`. The migration is dated today, after main's `2026_10_23_090000_users_made_by_editorial`, which had the same timestamp. The lock was rebuilt from main's: it adds `laravel/socialite`, `league/oauth1-client`, `socialiteproviders/manager` and `socialiteproviders/microsoft`, and moves nothing else.

**After merge.** The migration runs (`social_accounts`, `users.password_usable`). Nothing shows until a provider's client id and secret are in Forge. Setting each one up is in `docs/design/social-login.md`.

**Checks**
- `tests/Feature/SocialLoginTest.php`: 27 tests, #222's 23 with the two that joined on a non-held address updated, and new ones for: held and not held per provider, adding from the account page after a refusal, a new account on a non-held address, the holding page with and without a preview link, and the identity's own rule. The stubs now hand out whichever provider was stubbed last; before, a second stub in one test was silently ignored.
- 13 guards broken one at a time (each provider's rule both ways, `hd`, gmail, `xms_edov`, the controller's check, the cover, the preview link, the door): each failed a test.
- In Chromium against `php artisan serve` with the three providers configured: each button leaves for its provider with state and the right callback, the account page lists the methods, no horizontal scroll at 390 px, no console errors.
- Full suite 521/522. The one is `BuildStampTest`, which cannot read a branch ref from a git worktree and fails there on main too. Pint, ESLint and the Tailwind class lint pass.

**Not in this change**
- The privacy policy does not mention the providers yet; a sentence for section 2 is in the design note, for whoever signs off that text.
- The buttons are text only; Google's branding guidelines ask for its mark on a Google button.
params.title: Sign in with Google, LinkedIn and Microsoft (replaces #222): join an existing account only where the provider holds the mailbox
